title: Prompt Logging: what it uses
lede: One arrow for each component this feature lists. The steps reuse the feature's own "how it works" text; nothing here is a new claim. Internal and confidential: this text comes from an internal Ping deck and has not been tested on our tenant.

steps.title: Public key encryption of content
steps.what: Prompts and responses can be retained, encrypted with a public key you supply.
steps.why: Prompts and responses are exactly the content an investigation needs, and exactly the content a vendor should not be able to read.

steps.title: Private key entered at read time
steps.what: Only your private key opens them, entered in the console when you read a record, and Privilege never holds it.
steps.why: Prompts and responses are exactly the content an investigation needs, and exactly the content a vendor should not be able to read.

steps.title: Searchable metadata in the clear
steps.what: It is off until you turn it on: the usage record captures metadata only by default, prompt and response content is not written to the audit log by default, and full retention is an explicit tenant policy.
steps.why: Prompts and responses are exactly the content an investigation needs, and exactly the content a vendor should not be able to read.

steps.what: Agent Insights is the single place a security team goes to ask what happened: Guard results, Alerts and the prompt record across MCP, A2A, LLM and coding-agent traffic alike, filterable by agent, application, category, decision, flow and event.
